arguments.command:
python -c "
import glom
from glom import glom as glom_fn, Coalesce, Assign, Check, Let, Iter, Fill, Auto, Invoke, ROOT, constants

# Test R4 - Coalesce repr
print('Coalesce repr:', repr(Coalesce('a', 'b')))
print('Coalesce repr single:', repr(Coalesce('a')))

# Test R5 - Assign repr and assign function
print('Assign repr:', repr(Assign('a.b', 'value')))
print('Assign repr with missing:', repr(Assign('a.b', 'value', missing=dict)))

# Test R7 - Check repr
print('Check repr:', repr(Check(type=int)))

# Test R2 - New exports accessible
print('ROOT:', ROOT)
print('Let:', Let)
print('Iter:', Iter)
print('Fill:', Fill)
print('Auto:', Auto)

# Test R3 - Invoke and constants
print('Invoke:', Invoke)
print('constants:', constants)
print('consts:', glom.consts)

# Test new classes work
target = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}
result = glom_fn(target, Let('sum', ['a', 'b']))
print('Let result:', result)

target2 = [{'x': 1}, {'x': 2}]
result2 = glom_fn(target2, Iter('x'))
print('Iter result:', result2)

target3 = {'a': 1}
result3 = glom_fn(target3, Fill(0))
print('Fill result:', result3)

target4 = {'a': {'b': 1}}
result4 = glom_fn(target4, Auto('a.b'))
print('Auto result:', result4)

def add(x, y):
    return x + y
target5 = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}
result5 = glom_fn(target5, Invoke(add, ('a',), {'y': ('b',)}))
print('Invoke result:', result5)
"
